messages.content: Turn this into a polite request to my landlord: The geyser is broken again. Fix it this week.
Hello, the geyser in my flat has stopped working again. Could you please arrange for it to be repaired this week? Thank you.

Rewrite this in the third person. Ojas is a boy in Kavitha's class.

I'm Ojas, and I'm in Kavitha's class. At recess she stood by the wall alone. Then she went to our teacher and said something. I heard "nobody" and "play". The teacher called out, "Everyone, let's play statue!" and held Kavitha's hand. We all played. Kavitha laughed when she froze in a funny pose. I think she was sad before, but I'm not sure.

Ojas is in Kavitha's class. At recess she stood by the wall alone. Then she went to their teacher and said something. Ojas heard "nobody" and "play". The teacher called out, "Everyone, let's play statue!" and held Kavitha's hand. They all played. Kavitha laughed when she froze in a funny pose. Ojas thinks she was sad before, but he is not sure.
Simplify this for my grandmother, please: The pharmacy has notified customers that prescription refills must now be requested forty-eight hours in advance.
The chemist's shop says you now have to ask for your regular medicines two days before you need them.
Rewrite in the passive voice: The committee chose Farah as captain of the hockey team.
Farah was chosen as captain of the hockey team by the committee.

This is an old verse translation of the Ramayana. Please put it into plain modern English.

Then, with great joy that dame to meet,
The sons of Raghu clapped her feet;
And she, remembering Gautam's oath,
With gentle grace received them both;
Then water for their feet she gave,
Guest-gift, and all that strangers crave.

The two sons of Raghu were very happy to meet the lady, and they touched her feet with respect. She remembered Gautam's promise and welcomed them both kindly. She gave them water to wash their feet, a welcome gift, and everything a guest could need.
Could you turn this into the future tense? I pack my bag, lock the door and take an auto to the station.
I will pack my bag, lock the door and take an auto to the station.
Make this text to my friend less blunt: You're always late. I waited forty minutes. Don't bother next time.
I waited about forty minutes today, and I was a bit upset. Could we pick a time that works better for you next time?

Put this in the future tense, as a plan. "He" is Pradeep, a senior engineer.

He then made a list on the whiteboard: inspection, material order, rust removal, welding, painting, final check. Next to each he wrote a number of days, based on the old records. Then he added a week at the end.

He will then make a list on the whiteboard: inspection, material order, rust removal, welding, painting, final check. Next to each, he will write a number of days, based on the old records. Then he will add a week at the end.
Please write this in a formal tone for an email to the college office: hi, my fee receipt has the wrong name on it, can u fix it asap

Dear Sir or Madam,
My fee receipt shows the wrong name. Could you please correct it at your earliest convenience?
Thank you for your help.
Cut this down to one short sentence: In my personal opinion, I honestly think that we should probably leave a little bit earlier in order to avoid the heavy traffic.
I think we should leave earlier to avoid the traffic.

Join these diary notes into one flowing paragraph, without the day labels.

Monday. Arohi, five, noticed her Ammamma, Rukmini, lying down in the afternoon, which she never did. Arohi stood in the doorway, quiet, holding her doll.
Tuesday. Ammamma coughed a lot. Arohi brought her a glass of water without being asked and patted her hand. "Ammamma, sad?" "Just tired, kanna."
Friday. Ammamma sat in the garden again. Arohi drew her a picture of a sun with a smiling face and said, "For your cough to go away."

On Monday, five-year-old Arohi noticed her Ammamma, Rukmini, lying down in the afternoon, which she never did. Arohi stood quietly in the doorway, holding her doll. On Tuesday, Ammamma coughed a lot, so Arohi brought her a glass of water without being asked and patted her hand. "Ammamma, sad?" she asked. "Just tired, kanna," her grandmother replied. On Friday, when Ammamma sat in the garden again, Arohi drew her a picture of a smiling sun and said, "For your cough to go away."
Change it to the present continuous: Grandpa waters the tulsi plant while Riya feeds the parrot.
Grandpa is watering the tulsi plant while Riya is feeding the parrot.
Say this more confidently for my job interview: I'm not sure, but maybe I could possibly handle the accounts, if that's okay.
I am confident that I can handle the accounts well.

Shorten this to two sentences.

Francis came in again today to talk about internships. He had applied to four but had shortlisted thirty-one, and he showed me his notes on each. He said he had turned down an offer from a design studio last week because a friend, Vijay, mentioned a bigger firm might open applications soon. That firm has not opened anything.

Francis, who has shortlisted thirty-one internships but applied to only four, came in again today. Last week he turned down a design studio's offer because a bigger firm might open applications, but that firm has not opened any.
Rewrite this notice in plain English: Residents are hereby requested to refrain from parking vehicles in the vicinity of the main gate.
Residents, please do not park your vehicles near the main gate.
Make this sound more cheerful: The festival is next week. We have to clean the whole house and buy sweets.
The festival is just a week away! Let's get the whole house sparkling and pick out some lovely sweets.

How would this read in today's English? It is from the Panchatantra.

So the crocodile, having received his friend's advice, resolved to die if need be, said farewell to the monkey, and went to his own house. There he joined battle with the desperate ruffian who had forced a way in, put his reliance in resolute valor, and killed him. So he recovered his home and lived there happily for a long time.

So the crocodile took his friend's advice and decided to fight, even if it cost him his life. He said goodbye to the monkey and went home. There he fought the dangerous intruder who had forced his way in. He trusted his own courage and killed him. So he got his home back and lived there happily for a long time.
Put this into reported speech: Neha said, "I am going to the library because I need a book on volcanoes."
Neha said that she was going to the library because she needed a book on volcanoes.

Change the speech in this passage into reported speech.

Week three: At an alumni talk in the seminar hall, a former student named Mridul described working at a small robotics firm. After the talk, Abhinav's palms were sweating, but he walked up. "Sir, how did you get your first internship?" Mridul laughed. "Don't call me sir. Email me your project, I'll look." Abhinav went back to the hostel and wrote the email three times before sending it.

Week three: At an alumni talk in the seminar hall, a former student named Mridul described working at a small robotics firm. After the talk, Abhinav's palms were sweating, but he walked up and asked Mridul how he had got his first internship. Mridul laughed and told Abhinav not to call him sir. He said Abhinav should email him his project and he would look at it. Abhinav went back to the hostel and wrote the email three times before sending it.
Combine these into one smooth sentence: The train was late. We missed the wedding lunch. We still reached in time for the dancing.
The train was late, so we missed the wedding lunch, but we still reached in time for the dancing.
My boss needs this to sound professional: sorry boss, the report isn't done, my laptop died, will send tmrw morning
I am sorry, but the report is not finished yet because my laptop stopped working. I will send it to you tomorrow morning.

Rewrite these lines from Griffith's Ramayana in simple prose.

Right glad was Visvamitra when
He saw the prince of saintly men.
Low at his feet the hero bent,
And did obeisance, reverent.
Visvamitra was very glad when he saw the greatest of holy men. The hero bowed low at his feet and showed him deep respect.
Rewrite in the first person, as if Dev is speaking: Dev missed the bus, so he walked to school in the rain and arrived soaking wet.
I missed the bus, so I walked to school in the rain and arrived soaking wet.

Make this simpler for a younger reader, with short sentences.

The next morning Harish went with Santosh to meet the principal and showed her everything. She listened, kept copies, and called in the students' parents that week. When one teacher suggested moving Santosh to another section "to avoid trouble," the principal said no: "He did nothing wrong. They're the ones who'll change."

The next morning, Harish went with his son Santosh to see the principal. He showed her everything. She listened and kept copies. That week she called in the other students' parents. One teacher wanted to move Santosh to another class to avoid trouble. The principal said no. "He did nothing wrong," she said. "They are the ones who will change."
Make it kinder. I'm saying this to my six-year-old: Your drawing is messy and the colours are wrong.
I can see you worked hard on this drawing. Shall we try mixing some new colours together next time?
Remove the repetition: The movie was very very long and very boring, and the movie's ending was also boring.
The film was very long and dull, and so was its ending.

Write this in the first person, as Mohit telling it.

Mohit, nineteen, arrived in June from a small town. For the first weeks his room was full of instant-noodle packets and damp clothes left in a bucket. He came down twice to ask how to light the gas properly. He seemed embarrassed to be asking.

I was nineteen when I arrived in June from a small town. For the first weeks, my room was full of instant-noodle packets and damp clothes left in a bucket. I went down twice to ask how to light the gas properly. I felt embarrassed to be asking.
Explain it in words a ten-year-old could follow: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants convert sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen.
Green plants make their own food. They use sunlight, water and a gas from the air called carbon dioxide. From these, they make sugar for food and give out oxygen.
Rephrase so it sounds less like an order: Send me the photos from the trip by tonight.
Could you send me the photos from the trip sometime tonight, if you get a chance?

Shift everything here into the present tense.

Monday, Diwali week: Kishore, two, tried to stack five clay diyas. They toppled. He threw one.
Wednesday: His mother Rashmi held the bottom diya steady. Kishore stacked three, then shouted, "Done!"
Friday: Rashmi only rested a finger near the base. Kishore stacked all five. He danced in a circle, beaming at the whole family.

Monday, Diwali week: Kishore, two, tries to stack five clay diyas. They topple. He throws one.
Wednesday: His mother Rashmi holds the bottom diya steady. Kishore stacks three, then shouts, "Done!"
Friday: Rashmi only rests a finger near the base. Kishore stacks all five. He dances in a circle, beaming at the whole family.
Help me make this apology sound sincere: Sorry if you got upset about what I said.
I am sorry for what I said. It was unkind, and I understand why it upset you.

Please give me a modern prose version of this stanza.

His speech had scarcely reached its close,
When, as he stood, the sovereign rose,
And mounted swiftly to the skies
Before the wondering hermits' eyes.
He had barely finished speaking when the king, standing there, rose up and flew swiftly into the sky while the hermits watched in amazement.
Change these sentences to the negative: Kiran likes spicy food. She eats chillies every day.
Kiran does not like spicy food. She does not eat chillies every day.

Rewrite as just two sentences.

In a busy Madrid supermarket, Mateo, almost three, dropped flat onto the cold floor by the fruit. He screamed, kicked his shoes off and arched his back like a bridge. His dad, Sami, crouched down. "Mateo, listen, we'll..." Mateo threw a mandarin, then another. He couldn't hear a word. His cheeks were scarlet and his breath came in gulps. Sami moved the bag of apples out of reach and waited.

In a busy Madrid supermarket, Mateo, almost three, threw himself on the floor, screaming, kicking and throwing mandarins, too upset to hear a word. His dad, Sami, crouched beside him, moved the apples out of reach and waited.
For a shopkeeper, make this a polite question: How much is this? Give a discount.
Excuse me, how much does this cost? Is there any chance of a small discount?
Make this weather report easier to understand: Isolated thundershowers are likely over the coastal districts, accompanied by gusty winds.
There may be a few thunderstorms near the coast, with strong winds now and then.

Rewrite this so the toddler's words become full sentences.

On the steps of their Kolkata flat, Pooja held up her hand to Nikita, her mother, and showed a scraped palm. "Fall. Stairs."
"You fell on the stairs at Nani's?" Nikita asked calmly.
Pooja nodded. "Scared."
Nikita cleaned the scrape and blew on it gently. "Falling is scary. You told me, and now we've fixed it." Pooja watched her mother's face and relaxed.

On the steps of their Kolkata flat, Pooja held up her hand to Nikita, her mother, and showed a scraped palm. "I fell on the stairs."
"You fell on the stairs at Nani's?" Nikita asked calmly.
Pooja nodded. "I was scared."
Nikita cleaned the scrape and blew on it gently. "Falling is scary. You told me, and now we've fixed it." Pooja watched her mother's face and relaxed.
Write it in a warmer way for a thank-you card: Thanks for the gift. It was useful.
Thank you so much for your thoughtful gift. It has been really useful, and it made me smile.
Swap the passive for the active here: The cake was baked by Aunt Lily, and the candles were lit by the twins.
Aunt Lily baked the cake, and the twins lit the candles.

Modern English, please, for this verse.

Then Dasaratha, best of those
Whose speech in graceful order flows,
With gathered saints on every side,
Thus to the lord of earth replied:
"A truth is this I long have known,
A favour is the giver's own.
What thou shalt bid, O good and true,
We, as our power permits, will do."

Then Dasaratha, one of the finest speakers, with holy men all around him, answered the king: "I have long known this truth: a gift is the giver's to give. Whatever you ask of us, good and honest friend, we will do as far as we can."
Rewrite as yes-no questions: You have finished your homework. Your brother is coming with us. The shop opens at nine.
Have you finished your homework? Is your brother coming with us? Does the shop open at nine?

Make this teacher's note more formal for the school file.

Note from the class teacher. Yesterday Vishal and Usha argued over the puzzle. This morning Vishal sat apart with crossed arms, watching Usha build with blocks. At snack he told me, "I am still cross with her. But I want to play blocks." I did not push him to make up. After a while he walked over, held out a block and said, "Okay, let's play again." Usha took it, and I noticed his shoulders loosen. I will keep an eye on it.

Note from the class teacher: Yesterday, Vishal and Usha had a disagreement over a puzzle. This morning, Vishal sat apart with his arms crossed, watching Usha build with blocks. At snack time, he told me that he was still upset with her but wished to play with the blocks. I did not press him to make up. After some time, he went over, offered her a block and suggested they play again. Usha accepted it, and he appeared more relaxed. I will continue to monitor the situation.
Please tone down this complaint to the housing society: The lift is ALWAYS broken and nobody here cares!!!
The lift has been out of order quite often. Could the committee please look into getting it repaired soon?
Put it in the past perfect: Before the guests come, we clean the house.
Before the guests came, we had cleaned the house.

Put this bit of the Panchatantra into everyday English.

And the heron replied: "So long as I kept fat and flourishing by eating fish, I spent my time pleasantly, enjoying the taste of you. But a great disaster will soon befall you. And as I am old, this will cut short the pleasant course of my life. For this reason I feel depressed."

The heron answered, "As long as I stayed fat and healthy by eating fish, I had a pleasant life, enjoying the taste of you all. But something terrible is about to happen to you. Since I am old, it will also bring my pleasant life to an end. That is why I feel so low."
Make this sentence more vivid: The market was busy.
The market was packed with people, the air smelled of fried snacks, and sellers shouted their prices over the noise.

Rewrite so each sentence is short and simple.

On moving day the flat was full of boxes and noisy movers. Rehana, five, sat on the bare floor of her room. "Will my window come with us?" she asked her mother Zainab. "Will the tree be at the new house?" Zainab, busy taping a box, stopped and knelt. "The window stays here. I know you'll miss it. The new room has a different window." Rehana said nothing and held her sleeve for the rest of the afternoon.

It was moving day. The flat was full of boxes and noisy movers. Rehana was five. She sat on the bare floor of her room. She asked her mother, Zainab, "Will my window come with us? Will the tree be at the new house?" Zainab was taping a box. She stopped and knelt down. "The window stays here. I know you'll miss it. The new room has a different window." Rehana said nothing. She held her sleeve for the rest of the afternoon.
Make this shorter for a sticky note: Remember that you need to pay the electricity bill before the fifteenth of this month.
Pay the electricity bill before the 15th.

What would these lines sound like in plain present-day English?

King Janak's word the youths obeyed;
The maidens' hands in theirs they laid.
Then with their brides the princes went
With ordered steps and reverent
Round both the fire and Janak, round
The sages and the sacred ground.

The young men did as King Janak told them and took the brides' hands in theirs. Then the princes walked with their brides, in proper order and with respect, around the fire, around Janak, and around the sages and the sacred ground.

Can this line from the Ramayana be said in simple modern words?

He ceased: then Raghu's son replied
To the glad tale, and eager cried:
"Bring them with all thy speed: delay
No more, dear friend, but haste away."
When he stopped speaking, Raghu's son answered the happy news eagerly: "Bring them as fast as you can. Don't wait any longer, dear friend. Hurry!"
Can you make this formal for a leave application? I need 3 days off next week cos my sister is getting married.
I would like to request three days of leave next week to attend my sister's wedding. I would be grateful if you could approve this request.

Make this simpler, please.

At the bank's training centre in Pune, Tanuja, the coach, ran an odd exercise on the last day. Each trainee had to receive one compliment from the group and reply with exactly two words: "Thank you." No "but", no "it was nothing".

On the last day at the bank's training centre in Pune, the coach, Tanuja, tried an unusual exercise. Each trainee got one compliment from the group. They could answer with only two words: "Thank you." They could not say "but" or "it was nothing".
Rewrite in the simple past: Every Sunday we visit the lake and feed the ducks.
Every Sunday we visited the lake and fed the ducks.

Help me understand these lines by putting them in modern English.

Thus Visvamitra spoke the whole
To royal Janak, great of soul,
And when this wondrous tale was o'er,
The glorious hermit said no more.
In this way, Visvamitra told the whole story to the noble King Janak. When the wonderful tale was over, the great hermit said nothing more.
It's for my roommate, so make it gentler: Stop leaving your dishes in the sink. It stinks.
Could you wash your dishes soon after eating? They start to smell when they sit in the sink.

Please change the tense here to the present.

After the move from Porto to Lyon, Gabriel's French school felt like a wall of fast words. At home he stopped setting the table, a job he used to do proudly. He left his shoes in the hall and asked his father to cut his meat. And every night he padded into his parents' room: "Papa, I'll just sleep on the floor here."

After the move from Porto to Lyon, Gabriel's French school feels like a wall of fast words. At home he stops setting the table, a job he used to do proudly. He leaves his shoes in the hall and asks his father to cut his meat. And every night he pads into his parents' room: "Papa, I'll just sleep on the floor here."
Put the following in the active voice: The match was won by our school, and the trophy was handed over by the chief guest.
Our school won the match, and the chief guest handed over the trophy.
Turn this slang into standard English: Dude, the exam was lit, I totally aced it, no cap.
The exam went really well. Honestly, I think I did very well on it.

Give me this verse in everyday prose.

A thousand years had passed away,
When Brahma, Sire whom all obey,
Addressed in pleasant words like these
Him rich in long austerities:
"Thou by the penance, Kusik's son,
A place 'mid royal saints hast won.
Pleased with thy constant penance, we
This lofty rank assign to thee."

After a thousand years had passed, Brahma, the Father whom all obey, spoke kindly to the sage who had done such long, hard penance: "Son of Kusik, through your penance you have won a place among the royal saints. We are pleased with your steady effort, and we give you this high rank."
Simplify: Commuters are advised that the metro will operate at reduced frequency owing to scheduled track maintenance.
Metro trains will run less often because of planned track repairs.

Kavitha, a creche caregiver, wrote this. Rewrite it in the third person.

A cracker burst outside during snack time. Avni jumped and began to cry. Within a minute three other toddlers were crying or staring at her with worried faces; none of them had looked at the window.
I sat on the mat, took Avni on my lap and hummed our tidy-up song. The others crawled close. Soon they were quiet again.

A cracker burst outside during snack time. Avni jumped and began to cry. Within a minute, three other toddlers were crying or staring at her with worried faces; none of them had looked at the window. Kavitha sat on the mat, took Avni on her lap and hummed their tidy-up song. The others crawled close. Soon they were quiet again.
Please say this more politely to a waiter: Where's my food? It's been ages.
Excuse me, could you please check on my order? I've been waiting for a while.
Write this using "used to": When I was small, I played marbles every evening and collected bottle caps.
When I was small, I used to play marbles every evening and collect bottle caps.

Break the long second sentence into separate, shorter sentences. Leave the rest as it is.

In a Lyon cafe Aiko, two, began crying, loud and wet-faced. Felix checked: she was not hungry, having eaten her bread; she moved her arms and legs freely, so nothing looked hurt; she was not sleepy, since she had napped. Then the waiter lit the birthday candles at the next table and everyone sang. Aiko cried louder, then hid her face in Felix's chest and laughed. Felix could not be sure what she felt.

In a Lyon cafe Aiko, two, began crying, loud and wet-faced. Felix checked her. She was not hungry, because she had eaten her bread. She moved her arms and legs freely, so nothing looked hurt. She was not sleepy, since she had napped. Then the waiter lit the birthday candles at the next table and everyone sang. Aiko cried louder, then hid her face in Felix's chest and laughed. Felix could not be sure what she felt.
Join these with "although": It rained all day. We enjoyed the trip.
Although it rained all day, we enjoyed the trip.

Could you modernise this passage from the Panchatantra? Two ganders are leaving a dried-up lake, and the turtle is their friend.

When they did so, the turtle said: "Why do you bid me farewell? I am a water-dweller, and here I should perish very quickly from the scant supply of water and from grief at loss of you. Therefore, if you feel any affection for me, please rescue me from the jaws of this death. Besides, as the water dries in this lake, you two suffer nothing beyond a restricted diet, while to me it means immediate death. Consider which is more serious, loss of food or loss of life."

When they did this, the turtle said, "Why are you saying goodbye to me? I live in water. Here I will soon die from the lack of water and from the sadness of losing you. So if you care about me at all, please save me from this death. Besides, as the lake dries up, you two only have to eat less, but for me it means death straight away. Think about which is worse: losing food or losing a life."
Make this birthday message more grown-up for my manager: Happy bday!! Have a blast!!
Wishing you a very happy birthday. I hope you have a wonderful day and a great year ahead.

Rewrite this dialogue as a short paragraph with no quotation marks. Aparna is the one asking the riddle.

"Okay, riddle. Three friends ate lunch: one had rice, one had roti, one had noodles. Charu didn't have rice. Aparna didn't have roti or noodles. Who had noodles?"
Charu scratched her head. "Wait. Aparna didn't have roti or noodles."
"So?"
"So Aparna had rice!"
"And?"
"I didn't have rice... so I had roti or noodles. The third friend?"
"Didn't have roti."
"Then I had roti, and the third friend had noodles!"
Aparna clapped. "Step by step."

Aparna gave Charu a riddle. Three friends ate lunch: one had rice, one had roti and one had noodles. Charu didn't have rice, and Aparna didn't have roti or noodles. Who had noodles? Charu scratched her head and worked it out. Since Aparna didn't have roti or noodles, Aparna had rice. Charu didn't have rice, so she had roti or noodles. The third friend didn't have roti. So Charu had roti, and the third friend had noodles. Aparna clapped and praised her for going step by step.
Turn these notes into a full sentence: Library - closed Monday - reopen Tuesday 10 am - new timings.
The library will be closed on Monday and will reopen on Tuesday at 10 a.m. with new timings.
Reword this so it doesn't sound like blame: You messed up the concert booking, now we have no seats.
Something went wrong with the concert booking, and now we don't have seats. Let's see what we can sort out together.

Translate these old verse lines into simple English.

The mighty saint, with glory crowned,
With all the sages compassed round,
Praised by the Gods, gave full assent,
And Gods and sages homeward went.
The mighty saint, crowned with glory and surrounded by sages, was praised by the gods and gave his full agreement. Then the gods and the sages all went home.
Change to indirect speech: The coach told us, "Run three rounds and then drink some water."
The coach told us to run three rounds and then drink some water.

Put Salma's words into reported speech.

Note for Salma's parents, from her kindergarten teacher
Today we made birthday cards. Salma sat still for a long time. Then she said, "When Nani opens it, she'll smile. She likes roses. And yellow." She drew yellow roses. Harish asked why not a cake. Salma said, "Nani likes flowers more." I think she was imagining her Nani's face.

Note for Salma's parents, from her kindergarten teacher
Today we made birthday cards. Salma sat still for a long time. Then she said that when Nani opened it, she would smile, because she liked roses, and yellow. She drew yellow roses. Harish asked why she had not drawn a cake. Salma said that Nani liked flowers more. I think she was imagining her Nani's face.
Make this sentence positive instead of negative: The new park is not small and it is not far from our house.
The new park is big and close to our house.
Write this as a polite note to leave on my neighbour's door: Your car is blocking my gate.
Hello! Your car seems to be parked in front of my gate, and I can't get out. Could you please move it when you have a moment? Thank you.

I find this Griffith verse hard to follow. Rewrite it simply.

The hermit to his prayer inclined
And Janak, lord of virtuous mind,
With charges, to Ayodhya sent
His ministers: and forth they went.
The hermit agreed to his request. Then Janak, a good and wise king, sent his ministers to Ayodhya with a message, and off they went.

Tell this from the outside, in the third person, about Manoj.

Swati asked me at lunch why I'm always so tired if I got the job everyone wanted. I laughed it off. I shouldn't have. It's a good salary. My parents tell everyone. But today I spent eight hours making slides nobody will read, and the only good hour was when I helped the new intern understand the system. She said, "You explain so clearly!" and I felt more awake than all week.

Swati asked Manoj at lunch why he was always so tired if he had got the job everyone wanted. He laughed it off, though he felt he shouldn't have. It's a good salary, and his parents tell everyone. But that day he spent eight hours making slides nobody would read, and the only good hour was when he helped the new intern understand the system. She said, "You explain so clearly!" and he felt more awake than he had all week.
Rewrite this to sound casual, for a chat with my cousin: I regret to inform you that I will be unable to attend the family dinner on Saturday.
Sorry, I can't make it to the family dinner on Saturday.
Put it into the second person, as advice: People who save a little every week end up with a good amount by the end of the year.
If you save a little every week, you will end up with a good amount by the end of the year.

Turn this into three numbered points, one for each round of the game.

At the preschool's free-play hour, Indu hid behind the classroom door, and Pema, the seeker, opened the door and spotted Indu within seconds. Next round Indu tried the curtain by the window and lasted a little longer. The round after that, Indu wriggled under a nap-room cot and stayed hidden until the teacher clapped for a snack. Pema looked in three places before giving up.

1. Indu hid behind the classroom door, and Pema, the seeker, found her within seconds.
2. Indu hid behind the curtain by the window and lasted a little longer.
3. Indu wriggled under a nap-room cot and stayed hidden until the teacher clapped for a snack. Pema looked in three places before giving up.
Can you split this long sentence into three? My cousin Aisha, who lives in Pune and works as a nurse, came to visit us last weekend and brought a box of homemade ladoos that my mother loved.
My cousin Aisha lives in Pune and works as a nurse. She came to visit us last weekend. She brought a box of homemade ladoos, and my mother loved them.
Make this more encouraging for my younger brother: You failed maths again. Study harder.
Maths was tough this time, but I know you can do better. Shall we make a study plan together?

Plain English version, please. Sugriva is the Vanar king, and Rama has promised to help him.

Then glad was King Sugriva's breast,
And all his lords their joy confessed,
Stirred by sure hope of Rama's aid,
